metadata.description: Threat Log — adversarial findings from NIGHTMARE dream cycles.
metadata.notes: Deduplicated 2026-05-12: 20 raw entries collapsed to 4 canonical findings (5x re-emission per finding from cycle 676). A/B/D parked behind mcp-ext-auth dependency; C demoted to topology-only inference pending handler verification. Emitter dedup + lifecycle gate are open follow-ups.

threats.attack_vector: "Tool Execution Flow" accesses "Tools" (stores data) without visible auth/validation gates
threats.description: Potential privilege escalation: "Tool Execution Flow" → "Tools" path lacks authentication guards
threats.mitigation: Add authentication middleware between "Tool Execution Flow" and "Tools". Consider per-caller authorization on "Tools".
threats.ack_note: Latent risk: HTTP transport exists but is local/single-user today. Becomes real once VPS hosting + multi-tenant exposure ships. Re-activate alongside mcp-ext-auth integration.

threats.attack_vector: "Instance Registry Access Flow" accesses "Instance" (stores data) without visible auth/validation gates
threats.description: Potential privilege escalation: "Instance Registry Access Flow" → "Instance" path lacks authentication guards
threats.mitigation: Add authentication middleware between "Instance Registry Access Flow" and "Instance". Treat instance access as a tenant-isolation boundary once multi-user.
threats.ack_note: Latent risk under HTTP transport; tenant boundary doesn't exist yet. Re-activate with mcp-ext-auth.

threats.attack_vector: "Tool Execution Flow" accepts input and writes to "Tools" without visible validation
threats.description: Potential injection: unvalidated input from "Tool Execution Flow" reaches data store "Tools" via "related_to"
threats.mitigation: Verify (don't fix): MCP tool params already pass through schema validation at registration. Confirm against actual handler code before treating as actionable.
threats.ack_note: Topology-only inference from a `related_to` edge; heuristic did not inspect handlers. Confidence demoted from 0.55 → 0.30.

threats.attack_vector: Data entity "Instance" has no per-caller access control but is accessed by 1 entities
threats.description: Missing access control: "Instance" is accessible by [dreamgraph_instance_registry_access] without authorization hints
threats.mitigation: Reframed: implement instance-scoped authorization once multi-user. Original 'enable RLS' wording is Postgres-shaped and does not apply — Instance is a local JSON store, not a SQL table. Real remedy is per-instance ACL gated by the future auth layer.
threats.ack_note: Mitigation re-worded away from RLS. Re-activate with mcp-ext-auth.
